sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.title: Florida Joker gets his wish: He's a 'special voice actor' in Grand Theft Auto 6
sources.text: Looks like Lawrence Sullivan settled his differences with Rockstar. Remember in the closing days of 2023, when Rockstar dropped the first trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6 ? Amidst the everything it had going on was a brief shot of a man with extensive facial tattoos, who was quickly called out by people hip to such things as a knockoff of Florida Joker, aka Lawrence Sullivan, a Florida man who went viral for his 2017 mug shot . Sullivan himself called it out in a since-deleted TikTok video, first telling Rockstar " we gotta talk " and then, with no response forthcoming, threatening legal action . Not long after that, though, he put forth a new offer: " Let me voice the character , give me more storyline in the game… Let's make history happen, man." It seems that Sullivan got what he wanted: In a video posted to Instagram, Sullivan said he was given a role in GTA 6 . "I'm an official voice actor on GTA 6, the game." Sullivan says. "For the last three years a lot of people were saying I was not going to be in the game, I was not going to be nothing, they were destroying my mental health. They were saying a lot of fucked shit. But now it's time for me to shit on them and show them what the fuck Florida Joker is about!" "Y'all gonna see. Special voice actor for GTA 6. This ain't no gimmick, this ain't no lie!" I had doubts, but this apparently really ain't no gimmick or lie. Rockstar has posted the full GTA 6 credits and sure enough, Lawrence Sullivan is in there. Now, it could be a different Lawrence Sullivan, sure, but under the circumstances I don't think that's very likely. Sullivan's role doesn't appear to be a particularly prominent one: He's credited, along with a great many other people, as one of "The Local Population." But at the end of the day, he made it: Florida Joker really is in GTA 6, and he seems pretty chuffed about it. I'd call that a happy ending. sources.title: What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question
sources.text: "We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us." What would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors? That's the question Soldat and King Arthur's Gold developer Transhuman asked when it started working on 2024's roguelite shooter Maniac. The result is a delight, yet Maniac remains frustratingly underappreciated. Your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero. Throughout that time, your secondary objective is to create as much mayhem as possible - painting the road with the blood of your foes, slamming cars into buildings, performing drive-bys as you rampage across the procedurally-generated city. The more carnage you cause, the higher your Wanted level, until you're fending off police and the military. Maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock new characters, progressing a little further each time. It's a relatively slight experience, as its £4 price tag reflects, featuring a single compact map, just six characters, and barely any permanent progression. But Maniac makes a spirited argument for a return to a simpler time when GTA was all about shooting cops, stealing cars, and indiscriminately murdering pedestrians rather than the 'everything' game it is today. Maniac is also a game that feels like it's trying to make good on an idea many of us had when we first played GTA 1 & 2 all those years ago: what would a better-looking, more advanced version of that look like? And for developer Michał Marcinkowski, Maniac's genesis also harkens back to an earlier time. "When I was 12, I used to come back from school and play the demo of GTA 1," he tells me over email. "It was top-down and time-limited, and all I'd do was try to cause as much chaos as possible within the 20 minutes of the demo." And there's perhaps a hint of a 12-year-old's exuberance to Maniac. There's the bright colour palette and gleeful chaos of its physics-driven mechanics, the adrenaline rush its aggressive enemy AI creates, and its absurd roster of playable characters, which range from Little Girl to Hotdog Guy. "Each [character] is a bit of me and a bit of you," Marcinkowski explains. "We all have a drunk Santa in us. We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us. Each character failed at something and is lashing out." As each new Grand Theft Auto game pushes further into realism, the idea of recreating the rampages seen in classic GTA feels increasingly unpalatable, but Maniac's colourful cartoon aesthetic means it can get away with more. One Achievement, with a flourish of old-school bad-taste humour, challenges players to destroy five school buses using an airstrike ability called Santa's Little Helpers. And that level of irreverent, chaotic lunacy escalates the deeper into each session you get, particularly as your Wanted level climbs: if you antagonise law enforcement enough here, they eventually break out a game-ending nuke. "This comes back to being 12," Marcinkowski says. "Nukes are just cool. I wanted the game to end with a bang, and what's more maniacal and exaggerated than a nuke? So that idea was with me for more than 20 years." Core to Maniac's design is the ability to change from a Survivors-like auto-shooter to a standard shooter where you're able to control your aim. The latter option is, I think, the more fitting one, particularly given how much driving you do. If you squint, it almost feels like a GTA 2 clone. And while the Vampire Survivors inspirations are plentiful - including its now-standard three-option upgrade system - the GTA elements are clearly the more prevalent. It might not play exactly like a GTA game, but it certainly captures the series' early days spirit. And Marcinkowski says he's surprised more developers haven't tried to riff on GTA: "You'd expect the most popular game in the world to have hundreds of clones, but that's not the case." There may be a reason for that. As big as modern-day GTA is, clones are apparently much less popular. "When you look at the sales data, particularly of top-down GTA clones, they don't sell well", explains Marcinkowski. "I found that out way too late, and I thought Maniac wouldn't be a hit." His publisher was initially equally buoyant too. "But then they studied the market and stopped being so hyped. That's how it felt as we got close to release. The wishlist count wasn't very high." "I was expecting 10,000 [copies sold]," Marcinkowski tells me. "I actually started making another game two months before Maniac came out because I thought I'd go broke." But then the game launched, and early worries proved unfounded. It sold more than 100K copies, comfortably blowing past its maker's modest expectations, putting it in the top one percent of games released on Steam. It's a surprise success story built on the foundations of Marcinkowski's youth, and as we chat about GTA, he reveals he's less keen on Rockstar's modern games, which lack that classic gameplay drive. "I always liked the counter-culture side of GTA, which is why I put so much of it into Maniac," he elaborates. " GTA 6 seems to have become pop culture, so it's lost its appeal for me." Marcinkowski's heart, it seems, is old-school.

sources.title: Expedition 33 lead writer says Grand Theft Auto 6 layoff concerns show that 'people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value'
sources.text: "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing". Grand Theft Auto 6 is already enormously successful, having enjoyed "the biggest entertainment launch in history" . But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6 's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off." It might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one. It's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This issue was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July , claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 launches. "99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team." Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction." Svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector. "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created." sources.title: Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'
sources.text: Rockstar made a point of creating "authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality." It's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion. One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life. "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar ). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Humphries says this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6 , Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained. Establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world." This is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts . And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a 'complex drug network' that tracks everything from where drugs come from to 'how they eventually reach the street-level buyer'
sources.text: "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real." I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood. I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6 's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN , Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom. "A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer." Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there." While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. But it's such commitment to representing its world that has led GTA 6 to receive near-universal praise from critics, and it probably didn't hurt when it earned $3.79 billion on launch day , either. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. sources.title: How Rockstar Made Every NPC Feel Alive in GTA 6
sources.text: Game developers often refer to their open world cities as characters due to the sheer craftsmanship involved in building out a believable, diverse playspace for the player with its own districts, history, and architecture. This is truer for GTA 6 than most games, but what makes Leonida really feel alive — outside of the puddles of bin juice, the regional-specific cop cars, and mapped out power grid — are the people who live there. GTA 6 feels like a massive evolution in what it means to be a non-player character (NPC) because there’s an emphasis on the “C” — they’re actually characters in their own right. NPCs don’t just all look unique — with body types, skin, dress style, and hair making them stand apart — they have their own personalities and temperaments. Start a fight with one NPC and they might fight back, while another runs away. One could start a fight by slapping you, another might flick their cigarette at you or tip their drink over your head. Passersby can cheer the fight on, flee, or get involved. Some stop after a single punch knocks sense into them, while others swing until they’re out cold . No matter where you go in GTA 6, it feels like a lived-in world, on the macro and micro scale. There are over 100 interiors to explore, and each house tells you a story about its occupants. Listen to conversations out on the streets and you’ll get a window into their minds, built out by an entire Rockstar studio dedicated to making them authentic and believable, while still being larger-than-life, funny, and often unhinged. “A big part of it was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories,” said Steven Messinger, Rockstar's senior design director for the open world. “For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we’ve fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they’re distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer. “Players will only pick up on bits and pieces of this, but having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren’t there.” To build this tangible sense of place, Rockstar takes in-depth research trips for GTA games , embedding the writers in the mundane and the more extreme to really capture the soul of a city. Helicopter trips of the Florida Keys, ride-alongs with police, talking to people, taking photos and notes, all build up a snapshot that Rockstar bottles up to digitize in video game format. “We had a lot of fun trying to capture the raw energy and vibrant chaos that Florida is known for,” said senior design director of world and population, John Macpherson. “By immersing ourselves into a number of these locations on reference trips, spending time with locals, experiencing as much as possible firsthand, we gathered a direct sense of what would make Leonida feel truly alive. “Everywhere you look, little stories constantly unfold. It could be as simple as what someone’s wearing, how fit they are, how they walk and talk, who they’re with, what tunes they’re blasting as they cruise down the street. We tried to match that in-game as much as possible, hopefully resulting in something that feels full of life.” You can walk along Vice Beach and see sugar daddies with their trophy wives, locals playing volleyball, tourists sunbathing, and people walking their pets. Everywhere you look, there’s something happening in Leonida, and it’s completely enveloping. You feel like a part of its world, rather than a godlike being with total control over it. There’s a mission around the midpoint of the game where protagonists Jason and Lucia people-watch from a hotel sunbed, inventing backstories for the guests by the pool, and it’s something I found myself doing as I explored the world and passed people by, such is the variety and diversity of the game’s NPCs. No other game has ever had such a colorful cast of extras, which is wild when you consider all this was built to add credibility to a world you can zoom past at 100mph. “We evolved from monolithic NPCs built to visual standards that were lower than the main cast in GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, to fully fleshed-out characters with singular awareness and visual identities,” said Valmor Garcia, senior technical art director on GTA 6. “They are driven by dynamic moods, personalities, unique anatomy, facial features, and dialogue that are visually on par with our protagonists, Jason and Lucia.” Rockstar built entirely new technology for GTA 6 to simulate hair, cloth, and the way muscles move under the skin. All that work is implemented equally across all characters, so there’s never that uncanny moment where you come face-to-face with a flat and lifeless NPC, staring at you with dead eyes. Everyone you meet is equally detailed, and the range of visual design is staggering. Of course, this approach created challenges in other areas of development. It’s fairly straightforward to implement a combat system in a game where all character models are approximately the same size, but the varied body types of GTA 6 meant Rockstar had to take a look at how it approached animations so physical contact looks good no matter how big or small the character models are. Especially since this is a game where the two leads can also change in size through diet and exercise . “We decided early on that we wanted to really push the variation in character sizes and body types,” vice president of animation, Mark Tennant, explained. “This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat. “Developing this workflow meant that we needed our animators to adopt new tec

sources.title: The Binding of Isaac Dev Removes Undisclosed AI-Generated Music From Repentance+ Following Creator Response, Review-Bombing
sources.text: The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen. McMillen and Nicalis spent months building up to the November 19, 2026, release date for the latest update in their classic action roguelike game, but that launch was quickly soured. Just 8% of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent Steam reviews are positive, with a good chunk of comments left by players referencing AI-generated material that was not previously mentioned in any official capacity. "Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one popular review said . "I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds to refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," another said . "Shameful they would do this to an Indie gem. Shameful." The allegedly AI-generated content in question seems to be music exclusively tied to a specific, Grand Theft Auto-themed run meant to coincide with the recent release of GTA 6 . What could have been a cute jab at another gaming titan boiled into a full-blown controversy for Nicalis when Reddit user ShweetsStuff reported the questionable tunes just one day after launch. As artificial intelligence advances, it's become increasingly difficult to discern human-made art from content pushed out by machines, but ShweetsStuff was able to provide evidence backing their claims. Specifically, they pointed to a handful of tracks that mention AI music software Suno in their metadata, which also included links to their Suno pages. AI-generated content passed off as art has already become controversial on its own in recent years. Adding to the fire for The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was the fact that the music was featured in the new update without any sort of update to its Steam description. Valve requires developers to disclose how they may have used AI during game development, making the music's inclusion as puzzling as it is concerning for those who felt Nicalis had pulled the wool over their eyes. Negative reviews poured in following ShweetsStuff's discovery, leading McMillen to issue a statement today. He said he “had no idea" how AI-generated music found its way into the launch build of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s new update. "Woke up to a s**t show," he said , "obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned." Please report issues and bugs to the email attached. Just hours later, Nicalis launched a new patch, confirming the "removal of generated music files." The update is currently live for PC, with the studio adding that it has already been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony. When exactly it will go live for those platforms remains to be seen. No explanation for how or why the AI-generated music was included was provided. Instead, the team simply said it was "working on the game and will continue to address new and old bugs." McMillen also encouraged fans to report issues and bugs to the developers. In the meantime, The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent reviews on Steam remain firmly in the "Overwhelmingly Negative" category. The major update also coincided with the launch of Repentance+ on new platforms, including Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. For more, you can read IGN's 9/10 review for The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth and our 9/10 review for Afterbirth+ . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. sources.text: How to unlock and complete the alien UFO easter egg questline in Grand Theft Auto 6 Grand Theft Auto 6 is hiding an incredible alien easter egg, and it goes further than anything weâve previously seen in the series. Rockstar Games has always had a fascination with aliens and cryptids, and GTA 6 is no different. Only this one goes a step further and has a full alien questline for you to uncover if you keep your eyes open. In this guide, weâre breaking down how to start the new Alien UFO questline easter egg and the surprisingly amazing rewards you get for finishing it in Grand Theft Auto 6 . When itâs all done, youâll get The Truth Is Out There trophy and achievement. The first step is finding a car on the side of the road with its doors open and lights flashing. This will only happen at night, but can happen in a large variety of locations around Leonida. It will only be possible after starting Chapter 2. We found this first step of the alien questline while searching for all of GTA 6âs Meditation Spots. A good place to start looking is the quiet roads to the East of Port Gellhorn and North Kelly County. Thereâs no guaranteed way to spawn the encounter, but sleeping until night and driving around the darkest and quietest roads in Leonida is a good place to start. Once youâve found the car, youâll also find a trail of clothes leading away from it. Follow them, and youâll find a bright light with a naked woman hovering in the air. Interact with her to speak with her, and sheâll ask you to bring her car over. Try to, and your player character will have a close encounter before waking up in the same place during the daytime. Youâve been gone for three days. When you go to sleep as the protagonist who got abducted, you will eventually have a nightmare about being aboard the UFO. Inside, youâll first be greeted with the solar system in alignment. Inspecting Earth will show you a location that you can find in Leonida. Make note of the fenced-off, angular building, and the large tower, as those are the most recognizable bits of the scene. Next youâll find a keypad, and the solution is written above the keypad, only with lines instead of numbers. Two horizontal lines are a 2, four lines are a 4, etc. In our case, the code was â2431â, though it may change with playthroughs. In the next room is a light puzzle you must complete. You have access to four buttons connected to four lights, and each light has three stages: off, red, and blue. You must light them all blue to continue; only some of the buttons control more than one light. The buttons work as follows: Itâs an awkward puzzle to complete. You should aim to light all lights red, and then press the Second and Fourth buttons to activate them all once, turning them all blue. This will allow you to continue. This will allow you to access three doors. This mini-puzzle is simple: you must take the âmilkâ from the left room and place it in the machine in the right room. The center door leads to radiation that will damage you. Eventually, you will wake up from the nightmare, safe in bed. But you will wonder where the location shown to you in the dream actually is, and you can find it within Leonida. The building shown to you in the dream can be found in the swamp to the South of Hamlet, in Pelican Valley. Itâs just West of the main road leading North from Key Lento that goes over the Shoeless Keys. Finding it is pretty easy; getting in is harder, as the place is surrounded by barbed wire fences and gates that wonât open. Make sure to take a large vehicle, and then drive around to the rear of the building. Thereâs a metal structure that forms a path over the barbed wire fence, but youâll need leverage like a truck or van to jump on top and get inside the compound. You can use the nearby metal structures to climb up and over the metal rail, but it’s more difficult than it’s worth. Once inside, the character that was abducted will remark that this is the place from their dream, âthe place in the orbâ. Once inside, youâll find a door locked by a keypad, and youâll already have the code, as itâs the same as the one from your dream. Go down the elevator, and follow the linear path forward to find a control room with the same light puzzle from the dream, and the same three doors. Complete the puzzle and carry the milk precisely as in the dream, and the way forward will open. You will meet an alien. Like, no, actually. An alien in Grand Theft Auto. sources.title: GTA 6 Skunk Ape questline walkthrough: All effigy locations and choices
sources.text: How to start and complete the Skunk Ape questline in GTA 6 GTA 6’s Skunk Ape mission is one of the best side quests in the game, and rewards the player with a lot of cash, and a unique weapon. Jason teams up with a local weirdo named Kirk to track down a mysterious Bigfoot-like creature known as Mr. Mangrove. There are three missions in this questline. In this GTA 6 Skunk Ape guide, we’ve explained how to trigger the mission, the rewards for each section of the questline, and much more. So read on to find out how to start the Skunk Ape questline, and what you’ll get for completing it. Here’s how to complete every GTA 6 Skunk Ape mission, find the tree effigies and unlock all the available rewards. After you’re finished with Skunk Ape, if you need more GTA 6 guides? Then check out our GTA 6 Guide Hub . Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. To begin the Skunk Ape questline, find one of Kirk’s flyers advertising his search for the mysterious creature. These can be found at locations including Skeeter’s bar in Hamlet and the Rusty Anchor inÂ Key Lento, the game’s starting area. You can start this questline in Chapter 1, but you’ll need to progress to Chapter 2 to complete it. Or, you can start the Skunk Ape questline by encountering Skunk Ape in the open world. After this, Kirk will contact you. Once this happens, you’ll get a mission marker.Â Head towards Pelican River in Mariana County at night to meet Kirk beside his truck. Speak with Kirk and follow his drone into the swamp. It’s worth equipping your flashlight before heading into the woods, as visibility is limited. Eventually, you’ll reach a nesting site. Investigate the area and follow Kirk’s instructions before heading towards the feeding site. Examine the feeding area and inspect the claw marks on a nearby tree to the east. Kirk eventually spots Mr. Mangrove, triggering a chase through the swamp. You won’t catch the creature, but you’ll discover a strange wooden effigy attached to a tree. Inspect the carving and zoom in to examine it. A huge wild boar will then appear and charge towards you.Run back towards Kirk’s truck, marked on your minimap. The boar will knock you down, but Kirk intervenes and saves you. That’s the first part of the Skunk Ape questline in GTA 6 complete. After completing the first mission, wait for Kirk to contact you again. He’ll ask you to investigate additional carvings left behind by Mr. Mangrove. Travel to the search area in Pelican Valley, Mariana County, and locate three wooden effigies attached to trees. From my testing, there are mulitple possible locations that the effigys can appear, but you only need to inspect three to complete the objective. Below is where I found the effigys, but it’s possible that they appear in other dense bush areas. An airboat is particularly useful here, as several effigies are separated by waterways. Use your flashlight to search the trees and look for wooden carvings from the first mission. When you find an effigy, approach it and interact with it to examine the markings. Also, it’s probably easier to do this at night, since the orange glow that comes off the effigys is much brighter.Â Once you’ve inspected three tree effigies, the mission will end. The final mission, Help Kirk Find Mr. Mangrove becomes available after you reach Chapter 2. Wait for Kirk’s message and meet him near Cottonmouth Lake at night.Climb aboard Kirk’s helicopter to begin the hunt. He’ll provide a unique sniper rifle, the Mister Mangrove Laird 350. What makes this sniper unique is that it is a tranqulizer sniper, rather than blowing Skunk Ape to bits. Use the helicopter’s spotlight to locate Mr. Mangrove in the swamp. Once Kirk spots the creature, aim your tranquilizer rifle and fire several rounds at it. It doesn’t actually matter if you hit him or not, you’re essentially waiting for Kirk to get to the point where he’ll land the helecopter. Follow Mr Mangrove towards an abandoned shack and enter the building. Unfortunately, attempting to pick up Mr Mangrove exposes you to his strange pollen, triggering a hallucination. There’s no way to avoid this, so head towards Mr Mangrove to start the next part of the mission. You’ll temporarily control a frog and need to eat flies at three locations around the swamp. In order to find the flies, you need to find dead animals that are around the dock. If you’re struggling to find them, the minimap will start to point them. They aren’t massively aggro, but there are alligators while completing this section, so keep an eye out. After eating the flies, you’ll control a fly and need to return towards the helicopter. Listen to Kirk’s conversation with the pilot to discover the truth about Mr Mangrove and his real identity. The final encounter presents three choices: Regardless of your decision, the mission ends. If you shot Mr Mangrove, head back outside and watch Kirk take off in the helecopter with Mr Mangrove in the back of the helecopter. It’s well worth it.

sources.title: How to Get Ready for November 19
sources.text: November 19, 2026, has long been circled on your calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your XBOX console. We can hardly believe it’s almost here, either. Once midnight strikes, you want to be locked in the action, so to help you prepare, we created a checklist to ensure distractions are put to bed so you can settle in for a season of gaming like nothing you’ve ever experienced before. 2026 has been full of some absolute bangers: Gears of War E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Forza Horizon 6, Halo: Campaign Evolved, Minecraft Dungeons II, Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred , Control Resonant , Mixtape , Pragmata , The Blood of Dawnwalker , Star Wars: Galactic Racer , 007 First Light , Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve … seriously, all these games came out this year . That also means you might have a hard drive that is nearing capacity. And you will be faced with some hard choices to free up approximately 212GB of space on your XBOX Series X|S before November 19. You could always upgrade the capacity of your console to keep all your games at the ready, using the storage expansion slot on the back of the console. Otherwise, you’ll have a hard choice to make which we do not envy. But know that you’re in good company – we had to find a way to make room too. XBOX Cloud Gaming means that you don’t need to own an XBOX Series X|S console to experience the latest games (or use up that hard drive space) – you can stream directly from the cloud to your XBOX One console. Game Pass subscribers receive an allotment of hours per month as part of their plans, but you can also purchase blocks of time . Certain upcoming major releases have been confirmed as cloud-ready on day one , so even if you don’t own a current gen console, your latest obsession isn’t out of reach. You never want to settle in for a long gaming session only to immediately get hit with an update download. If you haven’t used your XBOX Series X|S or XBOX One in a minute, be sure to power up and connect to the internet beforehand and make sure you’re all set with the latest system updates. You can also install any upcoming releases you may have pre-ordered, while you’re at it. If you’re feeling a gaming flu coming on (and there’s a lot of that going around right now), then take a sick day, rather than risk infecting your coworkers or classmates. Sometimes you just need to listen to your body’s needs, relax, and let the fever run its course. Miami’s own DJ Khaled, aka Dr. XBOX will write you a personalized note to help explain the situation. If this thing is really serious, you may even need the whole week to recover – it’s the responsible thing to do. We all have responsibilities. Some of them come with four legs and a suspect bladder. Don’t let Rufus ruin your gaming fun. Get ahold of a local dog walker to take them outside so you can enjoy the big day uninterrupted. Or drop them off at doggie daycare for a day (or week) to get them out of your hair. Is your XBOX in an area of the house that is easily accessible to younger players? Consider the steps you need to take to get it out of younger sightlines, like running an extension cable out to the shed in the backyard or huddling up in your at-home office. Even if you do find yourself bouncing between rooms, your save files reside in the Cloud, allowing you to pick up your session wherever you last plugged your console in. We’re always on the hunt for new tunes and one of the things we’re most looking forward to on November 19 is discovering a whole bunch of new tracks that are sure to make our listening playlist pop throughout the year. You can get started here on Spotify . XBOX Design Lab lets you create your own next-gen XBOX Wireless Controller. Choose from a combination of colors, patterns, textured grips, and more. You could even pick up some specially themed versions of controllers styled in hot pink and pastels – this one is particularly striking . Speaking of controllers, if you expect long gaming sessions in your near future, make sure that it’s plugged in so it has a full charge when you need it, or stock up on AA batteries. Maybe even get a backup controller ready so you can hot-swap them in and minimize interruptions. Looking for something to add to your queue? Check out the 1967 classic, “Bonnie and Clyde,” featuring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway to get you in the mood for an epic story about two tragic lovers who fall into a life of crime. We’ll have to wait and see if the outcome is any different this time around starting on November 19.

sources.text: Finding the Slim Jim in Chapter 2 is essential if you want to get better at stealing vehicles Stealing cars in GTA 6 is one of the easiest ways to attract attention from the police, thanks to the new Wanted system. You've probably noticed by now that breaking into vehicles is noisy and messy, with Jason and Lucia needing to smash the window to get inside. It also takes time – precious time in which some nosey onlooker can report your description and activity to the cops. There has to be an easier way, right? There is. Which is why you need to learn how to get a Slim Jim in GTA 6. The Slim Jim in GTA 6 is only available from Chapter 2 onwards. This essential carjacking tool will unlock as part of the main GTA 6 mission list , coming into your possession after you begin a quest called ' Moses '. It's in this mission where you'll meet your first vehicle fence, learn how to sell cars and bikes in GTA 6 , and be given the information you need to better survey vehicles for security features with the WAiNK app – which can be activated at any time by holding Up on the D-pad. Moses will give you the Slim Jim as a part of this mission. It'll let you get into any vehicle without needing to smash the window. You will, however, still need to contend with security features – you'll have to wait until Chapter 3 to learn how to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 and understand how to deactivate trackers to steal more modern vehicles. Once you've got it, using the Slim Jim is GTA 6 is easy enough. Walk up to any vehicle you want to try and steal. Walk up to the driver-side or passenger door, and press Triangle/Y to bring out your Slim Jim. From there, it's a case of rotating the right thumbstick in a curve until you find the sweet spot – which you'll spot by rumble in the controller and by a slightly pink hue to the semi-circle indicator. Eventually you'll hear a little pop, meaning you can now climb inside. Find all of our GTA 6 Guides or scroll through below to find everything you need to know about vehicles in the game. sources.text: If you want to get in and out of a heist as fast as possible, here's how to get GTA 6 safe codes Finding and inputting GTA 6 safe codes is a slicker way to break into the 50+ safes scattered throughout the GTA 6 map . While some safes can be opened with sheer brute force, those that require a code often offer more lucrative rewards, so finding these safe codes can be a great way to make cash fast in GTA 6 . Unfortunately, these safe codes aren't always easy to come by. While some of the safe codes in GTA 6 are set – with those critical to the story and major side missions always consisting of the same digits– many of the codes are randomized and can change from player to player. So, while I can't give you the codes for those safes, I can at least help by guiding you on how to obtain them. So read on for tips on finding these randomized safe codes and for a list of set safe codes and their locations. There are two methods of getting GTA 6 safe codes: Which you'll need depends on the location, but by using your Focus by pressing down on L3 and R3/LS and RS, you can highlight the location of the safe code if there is one. If you can't see one, you probably need to threaten the staff by holding down the LT/L2 button and then press X/Square to threaten. Eventually, the threaten option will turn into a 'Safe code?' option, as seen in the image above. The Avery Pawn Shop GTA 6 safe code is an example of one of these, so why not use that to try it out. Alternatively, safes that require a code can be blown open using sticky bombs . These are only unlocked once you reach the Credit Checked mission in Chapter 3, but as I've explained in my dedicated guide to getting into the Kingpin Bowling safe in GTA 6 , there are a few you can pick up at the alley - and presumably other places around Leonida - before you unlock them at Ammu-Nation. These are the set GTA 6 safe codes that are the same for every player: Aside from the 0420 safe code that's given to you in Chapter 1, there are three main safe codes you'll need when gathering funds in GTA 6, and they're all related to the Kolt gang in Port Gellhorn. All three codes are found in the same place, Brooks Boatworks, but since they're set, you can use them from our list above without having to go looking for them. This won't save you a lot of trouble, though, as you'll still have to get past the gang in all three locations anyway. sources.text: The GTA 6 Snap Tool is an essential item which lets you get into locked doors without setting off alarms Breaking and entering is more complicated than it's ever been before in a Grand Theft Auto game. You never know what's behind a locked door – cash to be grabbed, narcotics to be fences, safes to be broken into. The problem is that breaking open doors creates a lot of noise, and will set off alarms. Thankfully, there is another way. All you need is to find the Snap Gun in GTA 6. The Snap Gun is a lockpicking device that can be acquired by progressing through the main story, and it's perhaps the most important piece of equipment in the game (beating out the Slim Jim and the Key Cloner ). Below I'm going to walk you through how to get the GTA 6 Snap Gun and how to use it. The Snap Gun is locked behind progression. You'll need to complete Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3, a fence-specific GTA 6 mission that unlocks after you've completed Boobie Time. You'll be introduced to Yasmani, one of the key vendors in GTA 6 who will pay a premium for marked bills and jewellery you've stolen. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that Jason and Lucia can properly assist in a few heists of high-end jewellery stores in Vice City. If a door is locked, there's a very good chance that you can use the Snap Gun to open it. Walk up to a door and, rather than pressing Square/X to break it open, press Triangle/Y instead. This will let you use the Snap Gun, where you're then required to use the left analogue stick to find the sweet spot and then pump the right-trigger until a meter fills. You'll hear the click when the lock is picked. The Snap Gun is particularly useful when you're robbing Pawn Shops, Jewellery stores, and other key locations – so long as you've already threatened the clerks and guards to stay still while you work. The Snap gun circumvents alarm systems installed in stores to monitor the door. It's worth noting here that in certain locations that carry a lot of cash or valuables, a Snap Gun won't be enough. If you walk up to a door and it's only asking for explosives, then a sticky bomb or grenade is what's required – just prepared for the alarms to go off and for the cops to be in hot pursuit. sources.title: How to get a GTA 6 Rhino tank and become virtually indestructible
sources.text: There are rows of GTA 6 tanks waiting to be liberated right from the start of the game, to earn the Challenging Tank award Getting a tank in GTA 6 represents the pinnacle of criminal behavior, and there's a long history of stealing Rhinos going all the way back through the series to GTA 3! These military vehicles are virtually indestructible so you're safely protected inside, and they pack a powerful enough punch with their cannon to destroy anything GTA 6 puts in front of you. You also need to get inside one to unlock the Challenging Tank Trophy or Achievement, so to help you out with that, here's how to steal a tank in GTA 6. The location for an entire row of GTA 6 tanks is in the Mile Zero Air Station, situated west of the area you begin the story in, which you can reach by driving through Abismo Key and on to Southwind. You'll need a vehicle to break into the military base which will get left behind, so it's best not to use your GTA 6 personal vehicle for this job, and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation is highly recommended for added protection. By following the route marked on my map above you'll weave through several road barriers, as which point the soldiers will open fire on you, then turn right at the first opportunity to pass more barriers and soldiers until you spot a handy pile of dirt. You must use this Stunt Jump to clear the perimeter fence, though if you don't get enough height to also clear the inner fence you can smash through it to reach the runway. Look to your left when on the miliary runway and you'll see a large building, and to the left of that are the Rhino tanks we're looking for – you can also head to the right of that building if you'd prefer to grab a GTA 6 jet instead. Once you reach the tanks, crash through the fence and then approach one before using the usual enter vehicle button to climb in through the front hatch. Note that there is various military hardware in this area, but the Rhino tanks are the ones closest to the fence you broke through. You can then drive away in your new GTA 6 tank, which will shortly unlock the Challenging Tank award from the GTA 6 Trophy and Achievement list to add to your collection. Strangely, commandeering this military vehicle doesn't initially increase your GTA 6 Wanted Level beyond the existing two-stars for breaking into the base, though this soon goes to five and then six-stars when you start blasting things with your cannon. Don't expect to get too far in your Rhino tank, as it drives pretty slowly and you're being constantly peppered with incoming gunfire plus rockets from helicopters – which you can shoot down if you aim your barrel high enough. However, the tank will eventually run out of fuel or become so damaged that it is completely incapacitated, and as surrender is no longer an option the upcoming Wasted is unavoidable. The Wanted Level you get won't affect your current GTA 6 criminal profile , though you can only get a six-star Wanted level in GTA 6 if you go all in on a psychotic rampage! sources.text: Arthur Morgan's genuine cowboy hat is found in a yard sale. Arthur Morgan's hat is found in GTA 6, a genuine cowboy hat that serves as a easter egg and reference to Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar's previous game and sibling franchise to Grand Theft Auto. Not just found on a hook somewhere, Arthur's Hat can actually be purchased and added to Jason and Lucia's wardrobe permanently - if you know the location of who's selling it. To get Arthur Morgan's brown leather cowboy hat for yourself in GTA 6, you need to go to a yard sale in the South of Port Gellhorn, found at the location marked above. The sale is marked by several very obvious balloons floating outside. Once there, head to the couch at the end, where you'll see a guitar case and a hat resting on it. That's Arthur Morgan's hat, though GTA 6 calls it a "Genuine Cowboy Hat" in Brown Leather. You can buy it from the owner, though the price seems to vary. When I bought it, it was $35, though some online have reported it being cheaper than that, suggesting the cost might be randomised. Once purchased, the hat will be in your wardrobe and clothing inventory permanently! For a little easter egg has the seller mention that she has no idea where the hat came from: perhaps she's a descendant of John Marston, the last canonical owner of that hat? sources.title: How to unlock the Cut-Off Tool in GTA 6 so you can open up those yellow Scoop containers
sources.text: If you want to get into yellow containers in GTA 6 to find secret vehicle stashes and weapons caches, you'll need the Cut-Off Tool first Have you noticed that there's these yellow cargo containers all over Leonida? Did you know that you can actually get inside of them to get rare weapons, explosives, vehicles, and so much more! It's yet another one of those hidden aspects of GTA 6 that you can't help but go out of your way to find more of, once you know to start looking. If you want to break into yellow Scoop containers in GTA 6, you're going to need to get a vital piece of equipment first: the Cut-Off Tool. Below I'm going to walk you through how to unlock the GTA 6 Cut-Off Tool and explain how it can be used to break into those Scoop containers. The Cut-Off Tool is one of the main pieces of GTA 6 equipment that you'll unlock as you play through the story. While you'll likely come across those yellow Scoop containers in your travels, you won't be able to open any of them until you've played a key GTA 6 mission in Chapter 3. Meet the Heders is the third mission of that chapter, and it'll send you down to a dockyard. Once you're these, you'll automatically be assigned the equipment and can use it freely outside of the mission. You need to locate yellow Scoop shipping containers. These can be in the most unlikely of places – on random beaches, next to gang hideouts, in random parking lots – all across Leonida. Once you've located one, walk up to its front doors and press Triangle/Y. This will prompt Jason or Lucia to equip the Cut-Off Tool. You'll need to squeeze R2/RT and keep the power within the pink segment of the semi-circle for a short while until you cut through the lock. Once you do, the doors will swing open and you're welcome to whatever you find inside. Have more questions you want answered? Then visit our GTA 6 Guide and Walkthrough hub for more essentials. sources.title: Can you free-roam after beating GTA 6?
sources.text: You can keep playing GTA 6 after the credits, but there's some things you may want to know first No matter how far you're through the main GTA 6 missions list , you are probably starting to get a sense of just how massive Leonida really is – and how stacked it is with curiosities, distractions, objectives, and side-activities. So naturally you must be wondering if you can free-roam after beating GTA 6, or whether you need to pack everything in before hitting a point of no return. I'm going to answer this question for you and, because I'm nice, I'm going to do so in the most spoiler-free way that I possibly can. You can continue free-roam after beating GTA 6 , albeit with a few caveats. Because there are numerous GTA 6 endings, with a wide range of different variables and impacts for all of the characters depending on your relationship status , your criminal profile , whether you paid into family savings , and plenty more besides, Rockstar has decided that it would be far too difficult to simply drop you back into Vice City in a world in which there are no more main missions daunting your GTA 6 Index . This means that once you've completed the main story in GTA 6, the game will drop you back to an auto-save just before the point-of-no-return. When the game does this, I recommend that you be prepared to make a new save in GTA 6 – as that auto-save won't exist forever, and can be lost if you decide to load an old save or start the campaign over from scratch. From this point, you're free to do whatever you want to do. Your relationship status will be locked, so there's no need to worry about maintaining this if you don't want to, but you can still mess around with your Criminal Profile. You can also, at any point, restart the final mission and go through it again. The GTA 6 end-game is where the world really lets you be free. You'll have loads of GTA 6 challenges to complete, which contribute to the unlocking of GTA 6 Cheats that are now available in the Progress menu. So, long story short, you can free-roam after beating GTA 6, but expect to have that final mission sitting on your menu screen for the long haul. Looking for help in Leonida? sources.title: GTA 6 Triggers Busiest Traffic Day in Comcast History
sources.text: Comcast has said GTA 6 's launch triggered the busiest traffic day the company has seen since it was founded in 1963. The latest record broken by Rockstar Games' latest actually comes from one of the biggest media and technology companies in the United States. After previously reporting that Grand Theft Auto had led to a 4x increase in traffic on Xbox consoles November 18, Comcast has now confirmed that pre-loads for the day resulted in the busiest day it has ever seen – and it wasn't close. Comcast recorded peak traffic 31% higher than the average day and 9.6% higher than the previous record holder. Moreover, GTA 6 has resulted in five out of 10 of the busiest days the network has ever seen. Even more remarkable is the news that, as reported by Comcast, 24% of all of its internet traffic during peak times was from users downloading and playing the game. If Rockstar fans weren't playing GTA 6, they were watching it. Twitch traffic increased by almost 50% on November 18 and is continuing to rise in the days following that launch. GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, but thanks to the New Zealand trick , a massive chunk of players actually took their trip to Leonida hours early. It certainly helped boost traffic across the board, and in Comcast's case, it resulted in its busiest day ever. To put some of these numbers into perspective, the company shared a very relevant measurement. November 18 traffic generated on PlayStation and Xbox alone delivered enough data for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K… for two days straight. It's shocking to see how GTA 6 affected Comcast, but then again, we've known Rockstar's new game would be a juggernaut when it eventually launched. The developer's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, reported that it had earned an unbelievable $3.79 billion in the first day after its release. That makes it not just the biggest video game launch of all time, but the biggest entertainment launch across any medium . Critics everywhere helped GTA 6 earn the title of highest-rated game of all time . IGN was included in that list after delivering a 10/10 review . We said, "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played." sources.text: November 19 marked the highest-traffic day in the ISP's history. In a post to X, "The Everything App," US entertainment and communications conglomerate Comcast revealed that Grand Theft Auto 6 's historic launch drove record-breaking internet traffic. According to Comcast, only a quarter of "the entire internet" was downloading Rockstar's latest cozy game phenomenon . "GTA 6 didn't just break records in gaming," Comcast wrote. "Its launch drove the biggest internet traffic day in our network history, with traffic climbing 31% above an average day. At peak, GTA 6 accounted for nearly a quarter of all network traffic." Comcast shared a video of a line graph showing the massive relative spike in activity on November 19. The chart is unlabeled except for the date, but it presumably corresponds to the volume of data being downloaded across Comcast's entire network. And that last but does add a caveat to the numbers Comcast cited: Its network and "the entire internet" are two different things, unless I'm missing something here or Comcast's data accounts for other ISPs and other countries, not just its own services. Regardless, it's still a significant bit of fun with statistics, another example of the totalizing footprint of what may be the largest commercial launch in entertainment history .
